findings.title: Data race fix ships without a regression test
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race on the global entryPointAssetsCache but adds no test to verify the fix or guard against future regressions. A small concurrent test (e.g. many goroutines calling GetWebAssets in a loop with t.Parallel, or any test invoking it under `go test -race`) would have caught the original race and now lock in the fix. Without it, the cache mutex can be removed in a future cleanup and the race will silently reappear.

findings.title: Incomplete double-checked locking causes redundant manifest reads and serializes dev-mode calls
findings.body: After taking the RLock, the code releases it and then takes the write lock without re-checking the cache. Two consequences: (1) in non-dev mode, concurrent cold-start requests each block on the write lock and then each read the manifest file from disk; the second reader does no fast-path re-check and re-does the I/O. (2) in dev mode, every call bypasses the cache and re-reads the file, but now all dev-mode calls also serialize on the write lock instead of running in parallel as before. Adding a re-check inside the critical section (e.g. `if entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`), or replacing the RWMutex with sync.Once / atomic.Pointer[dtos.EntryPointAssets], would remove the redundant I/O and the dev-mode serialization.
